text: So some horrific stats have come out this week from a University of New South Wales study which showed that one in five men have had sexual feelings towards children, and one in five men have actually offended against a child. What do you imagine when someone tells you one in five men have had sexual feelings towards children and have offended against a child? You probably pictured the worst possible image. A grown man and a very young defenseless kid, maybe around 10 years old. It's a horrible image, it's a terrible problem, and it's absolutely worth talking about. But now you hear that stat and you think, wait, one in five men are like that? And if you scroll the comments under that video, every other person is saying it's even worse. It's one in two, it's four in five, it is higher. Look, any normal man's blood starts to boil when he thinks about predators out there hunting and attacking kids. It's a horrible crime, one that we should be taking very seriously. And research like the one this guy is quoting is genuinely important work. It is real research by real academics looking at a real problem. But the issue starts when people take serious research and twist it. So let's actually look at what the study said. The number comes from a 2023 report out of the University of New South Wales in Australia, led by Professor Michael Salter. It surveyed 1,945 Australian men through an online panel, asking anonymous self-report questions about their attitudes, attractions, and behaviors involving people under 18. By the way, three years ago, not this week, as the video states. And the headline figure, the one in five, does exist in the report. But it doesn't mean what the guy in the video claimed. He said, one in five men have had sexual feelings towards children, and one in five men have actually offended against the child. But this is simply wrong. The report shows that 15.1% reported the feelings, and 9.4% reported what the study calls offending. Neither of those is one in five, and only 4.9% reported both. Still horrible numbers. Most people would hope it would not be bigger than zero. But it is lower than what the guy stated in the video. And this is my issue. The numbers are alarming enough on their own. You do not need to inflate them. You do not need to lie on top of them. You do not need to turn them into an agenda to vilify a bigger share of men. Men who are just as disgusted by this problem as the next person. Misinformation and blaming men will not raise awareness. It will make things worse. If you actually care about the issue, then you should care about informing your audience with correct information. And this is what I want to do here. I want to get the message across the right way, and walk through some other things in this study that need to be highlighted. Here's the first issue. When you hear the word children, you probably picture young kids. This is not how the study defined it. The researchers themselves defined children as anyone under the age of 18. A 17-year-old, a 16-year-old counted the same as a 6-year-old. Now, by itself this may not be an issue, but the age of consent in Australia is 16 years old. So a consensual and legal activity between a 19-year-old and a 17-year-old could still be counted in this study as sexual contact with a child. That is important context for how we read the results. Second issue. When you hear offended against a child, you probably picture some type of physical abuse. That is not exactly what the study measured. The study counted five behaviors as offending. Things like flirting online with someone under 18, viewing adult-rated material containing someone under 18, webcamming. Most of it is online behavior, not physical abuse. And a man only needed to say yes to one of these things to be counted. These behaviors can range from worrisome to outright disgusting, but they are not what most people picture when they hear sexual offense against children. For me personally, if I had to pick out the most worrying numbers from this study, they would be these. 5.7% would have sexual contact with a child between 12 to 14 years if no one would find out. 4.6% would have sexual contact with a child between 10 to 12 years if no one would find out. 4.0% would have sexual contact with a child younger than 10 years if no one would find out. Yes, those are only hypothetical questions, but the reported numbers are terrifying nonetheless. As a society, we should be talking about them. We should be doing something about them. But we shouldn't be inflating them to make them look more sensational for social media. The numbers are already alarming on their own. Misrepresenting them does not protect kids. It doesn't raise awareness. It just gives some people a reason to dismiss the next study that comes out. And it paints a much bigger portion of men as predators when most of them are just as disgusted by these numbers as you are.
